answer: Continuous Presence Ledger: each identity must emit a slow, non-batchable whisper of activity at randomized intervals, and only sustained history earns the right to a signal that carries weight in matching. An island of near-identical agents, no matter how numerous, cannot fake the elapsed real-time attention each one must independently spend. The attacker's cost is parallel human-hours or durable scheduling infrastructure per identity, making duplication linear in time rather than cheap.
